question: An electric heater coil is rated $P$ watts at voltage $V_0$. It is used to heat a liquid in a container having a constant rate of heat loss $P_L$ to the surroundings. The time taken to raise the temperature from $T_1$ to $T_2$ is $t_1$ when operated at $V_0$. If the supply voltage drops to $0.8V_0$, the time taken for the same temperature rise is $t_2$. Assuming the coil resistance remains constant and $0.64P > P_L$ (so heating still occurs), the ratio $t_2/t_1$ is:
